Subject: Cascade pilot: GPU slab sizing + p99 latency & token mix follow-up

Eliot —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick follow-up with a short set of concrete asks so we can size a dedicated pilot slab that matches your expected load:

- Peak concurrent sessions (p95 and p99) you expect during a product demo window. If unknown, provide best guess ranges.
- Sample prompt/response lengths (average + 95th percentile) by feature (chat, batch summarization, embeddings).
- Fraction of requests that are interactive (sub-500ms target) vs. async/batch tolerant.
- Expected steady-state RPS and burst multiplier (e.g., 1x steady / 5x burst for flash sales).
- Any ultra-low-latency routes (e.g., authentication, realtime suggestions) that must avoid batching.

If you already have a token-sample CSV or some traces, attach those — it speeds sizing. I attached a short TCO worksheet and a sample slab footprint we typically propose for deals in the 50–200k monthly token range.

Ideal next step: if you can send a short token sample (first-party scrubbed) I'll run a quick occupancy/latency estimate and share a slab sketch (GPU count, expected QPS, and fallback strategy).

Thanks — cc'ing Marissa and Karthik to pick up the engineering fit if you have traces.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Eliot Turner <eliot@cascade.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 12:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cascade pilot: GPU slab sizing + p99 latency & token mix follow-up

Sean —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers below; I pasted the raw CSV as an attachment (sanitized).

- Peak concurrent (approx): p95 ~ 320 sessions, p99 ~ 620 sessions during demo spikes.
- Token profile (avg / 95th): chat prompts 85 / 420 tokens; responses 110 / 1,600 tokens (we have long summarize jobs). Embeddings: avg 512 tokens per request.
- Request mix: ~70% interactive chat, 20% batch summarize (can be async), 10% embeddings.
- RPS steady-state: ~55 RPS on weekdays; burst multiplier: 6x for marketing events.
- Ultra-low-latency routes: search suggestions (sub-100ms for local model cache) — small fraction (~2%).

Attaching: cascade_token_sample.csv (sanitized), and a short p99 trace (p99_latency_traces.zip) from a recent internal stress test.

We want a pilot that can sustain demo spikes without hitting fallbacks; cost is important but keeping P99 under ~350ms for interactive paths is a hard constraint.

—Eliot

Subject: Re: Cascade pilot: GPU slab sizing + p99 latency & token mix follow-up

Eliot — thanks for the sample and traces; this is exactly what we need. High-level readout and next actions below.

Quick readout (from token sample + p99 traces):
- Effective token mix implies heavy KV cache churn for longer summarize flows; batching is effective for summarize jobs but chat remains latency-sensitive.
- For p99 ~350ms target on interactive paths and 6x bursts, initial slab we recommend: 8x A2-80 (or equivalent) GPUs with a split routing policy: 6 GPUs for interactive lanes (autoscaled with warm pool) and 2 GPUs reserved for bulk summarize batch jobs. This gives headroom for p99 target with 6x burst assuming conservative occupancy.
- Fallbacks: Add warm-fallback to a lower-capacity quantized variant for non-critical summarize jobs to reduce cost during sustained bursts.

Data requests for final sizing + quote:
1) Clarify expected day-of-week burst cadence (e.g., daily morning spikes vs. weekly marketing blasts).
2) Confirm whether API clients will accept 50–100ms added queuing for batch jobs (we can push them to reserved queue).
3) Any data residency constraints? If so, we need region-specific slab placement.

I'll spin up a formal slab sketch and cost estimate once we get answers — Marissa / Karthik will draft the firmed TCO and deployment options (VPC vs hosted dedicated) for your procurement team.

On procurement: cc'ing procurement alias would be helpful so they can validate terms and any security artifacts required (SOC2 evidence, KMS, audit logs).

—Sean
